list: the official 55 trophies, checked 2026-11-19 against Exophase and PSNProfiles (names, descriptions and grades agree on both)
counts_from: PSNProfiles trophy targets (0/N shown on each counted trophy), opened 2026-11-19
hidden_note: PlayStation lists 28 of the 55 as hidden. The per-trophy hidden flags below follow the 28-name hidden table in the EGamers.io trophy list (opened 2026-11-19), which matches the 28-hidden total on Exophase and PSNProfiles: every story/chapter/mission trophy, the five side-character finals, Fair Game, the two airport/tank stunts, the three vague venue trophies, the four vague story-moment trophies, and Ten Pin. Sneakthief is not in that hidden table, so it is marked visible.
honesty: Grand Theft Auto VI had just released when this guide was written. Every guide below is derived from the official trophy description plus the cited sources; no step has been verified inside the game yet. Where a trigger is still unconfirmed, the guide says so instead of inventing one.
app_disclaimer: Pre-release planning guide. Instructions are derived from published trophy descriptions and cited sources. Gameplay, replay access, missability and completion time have not been verified in-game.
verification: All 55 names/descriptions/grades checked against Exophase and PSNProfiles (opened 19 Nov 2026, both agree). Grade totals: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze. Hidden flags: exactly 28 true, following the 28-name hidden table in the EGamers.io trophy list (opened 19 Nov 2026); the text extraction of Exophase/PSNProfiles did not expose per-trophy hidden markers, so the EGamers table is the source for which 28 — recorded here, not silently chosen. PSN targets (0/N) read from PSNProfiles. Discrepancies recorded, not resolved silently: meditation spots 18 (PSN count) vs 15 (100% checklist); Fair Game animal unconfirmed; triggers for In The Beginning…, Capital Offense, Bad Luck, I Guess, The Truth Is Out There and Ten Pin unconfirmed.
schema_note: Per trophy: id, name/description/grade exactly as published, guide in our own words, hidden (bool) + hidden_note above, spoilerCategory = kind story (spoiler masking keys off kind, not the hidden flag), kind (story/collectible/activity), tags via kind + grade, target (PSN count value + target_unit, null when the trophy has no count — never 0), missable (bool) with missable_reason; the app renders the honest missability label from these fields (app/js/views/detail.js missabilityLabel): potential for the one flagged trophy, ending-related for the final mission, trigger-unconfirmed where the guide says so, otherwise no specific signal. chapter/mission only where the description states it, else null. sources[] carry name + URL; what each source supports is rendered by the app (name/description/grade, PSN count, early-guide detail). State (earned, counters, notes) lives separately in localStorage, never in this file.

PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI Trophies

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.missable_reason: Cannot be missed: it pops automatically once the other 54 are earned.
trophies.guide: This is the platinum, and it needs nothing of its own: earn the other 54 trophies and it unlocks by itself. Treat it as the finish line of the roadmap, not a trophy to hunt directly. The last trophy you earn will almost always be the 100% completion gold, A Long Road, so plan your cleanup around that.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.missable_reason: Story trophy: unmissable, it comes from playing the opening mission.
trophies.guide: Play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, to the end and the trophy pops when it completes. There is nothing to prepare and nothing to collect first; it is the game's first story beat. If you are following the roadmap, this is step one and it cannot be skipped.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.missable_reason: Story trophy: unmissable, awarded for finishing Chapter 1.
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1 and the trophy unlocks at the chapter's end. Before you move on, it is worth clearing any activities Chapter 1 opens up, since later chapters add more to juggle. Nothing in Chapter 1 is flagged as missable by the sources we checked.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.missable_reason: Story trophy: unmissable, awarded for finishing Chapter 2.
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 2 in full. This chapter is where both protagonists become playable together, which opens the partner activities behind Hot Together and Retail Therapy, so try a co-op moment here rather than leaving both for the endgame. The trophy itself needs only the chapter's last mission.

trophies.missable_reason: Story trophy: unmissable, awarded for finishing Chapter 3.
trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 3 to its final mission. By this point the map is largely open, so it is a good moment to bank progress on the long counters — vehicles discovered, stunts, WAiNK spots — instead of rushing the story. The trophy pops at the chapter's close either way.

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4 and this trophy unlocks at the chapter end. trophies.missable_reason: Story trophy: unmissable, awarded for finishing the final mission.
trophies.guide: Complete the final story mission and this gold trophy pops. Do not treat the credits as the end of the hunt: after the story, free roam stays open for the collectible and activity trophies, and 100% completion is a separate gold. Save before the final mission if you want a clean rollback point for any choice-tied trophies.

trophies.missable_reason: Story mission trophy: unmissable as long as the mission is completed; missions can be replayed if needed.
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Breakfast Run. It unlocks during the campaign, so just keep playing the story and it will appear in your mission list. The name suggests an early, low-stakes job — expect a drive-and-deliver style mission rather than a big set piece. No special preparation is needed.

trophies.missable_reason: Story mission trophy: unmissable as long as the mission is completed.
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heists in this series are usually multi-stage, so stock up on ammo and armour before you start it, and expect the trophy at the mission's end screen. This is also good practice for the later robbery trophies, which reuse the same escape-and-evade rhythm.

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The operation-style name suggests a large, combat-heavy mission, so go in with full health, armour and a stocked weapon wheel. The trophy unlocks when the mission ends, with no extra objective named in the official description.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.missable_reason: Cannot be missed: 100% completion stays available in free roam after the story.
trophies.guide: Reach 100% on the game's completion checklist — PSN tracks it as a 0 to 100 counter. In this series that checklist covers story missions, stranger strands, activities, collectibles and the big counters on this list, so this gold is really the sum of everything else. Leave it for last: it should pop naturally once the other grind trophies are done, and the in-game stats page shows what is still missing.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.missable_reason: Cannot be missed: stunts stay available in free roam; PSN tracks 0/250.
trophies.guide: Land any 250 stunts — PSN tracks the count, and early guides report there are 397 stunts in total, so you do not need them all. Flying under bridges is reported to be the quickest kind of stunt to repeat. Work on this passively while travelling: every bridge you fly under and every jump you land counts, and the counter in this guide lets you track your running total.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.missable_reason: Cannot be missed: activities stay available in free roam; PSN tracks 0/9 types.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once — PSN tracks the count as 0/9, so sampling is enough and you do not need to master any of them. The activities include the ones named elsewhere on this list: fishing, drone racing, arcade games, bowling, shooting range, racing, hunting and meditation, plus one more to discover. Dip into a new activity whenever its icon appears on the map and tick it off here.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.missable_reason: Cannot be missed: shooting range challenges can be retried as often as needed; PSN tracks 0/42.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges — PSN tracks the count as 0/42. Treat it as a skill grind, not a one-shot test: every challenge can be retried, so learn each range's target pattern, pick the weapon the challenge favours, and chase gold one range at a time. This is one of the six silver trophies and a long one, so start early and return between story missions.

trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations — PSN tracks the count as 0/14, and early guides count 42 races across those locations, so each site hosts several races and you only need one win per site. Learn the course on a practice run, then race to win; a win at a new location is what moves the counter. Keep a note here of which locations you have already won.

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — PSN tracks the count as 0/20, and the word different matters: replaying the same race does not add to it. Spread your wins across race types and locations, and use the fastest vehicle you own for each one. Note that the 100% checklist reportedly asks for 30 race wins, so this trophy stops short of the full grind.

trophies.missable_reason: Cannot be missed as far as the sources say: a fishing challenge against Cal that can be attempted again.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing is one of the game's activities, and Cal is the rival angler you face in it — challenge him at a fishing spot and out-fish him in that round. If you lose, try again: the trophy is about winning the challenge once, not about a perfect catch. A better rod and a calm approach to the reeling rhythm should help; the exact mechanics are not yet verified in the game.

trophies.missable_reason: Cannot be missed: can be attempted any time both protagonists are playable together.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, reach a 4-star wanted level, then lose the cops and escape the red heat zone on the map. Early guides point to a train tunnel north of Ambrosia as a good escape route, and note that bank vault robberies often bring on the wanted level you need — so pair this with Maximum Withdrawal. Make sure your partner is with you before the heat starts, or the trophy will not count.

trophies.missable_reason: Cannot be missed: can be attempted any time both protagonists are playable together.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops in a row while staying wanted the whole time — losing the wanted level between robberies breaks the chain. Early guides suggest the jewelry stores in North Vice City, which sit close together, and advise robbing a fourth shop if the trophy does not pop after the third. Plan a short route between three nearby shops before you start, keep your partner close, and move fast.

Early guides report you discover a vehicle by scanning it with WAiNK, with no need to drive it, and that scanning traffic near busy roads is efficient. So keep WAiNK ready in traffic: scan every new model you see, and the counter climbs without you ever getting behind the wheel.

Early guides advise filling your Focus meter before the fight starts, using an assault rifle, and aiming for gang members — cops, soldiers and civilians reportedly do not count. trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure from VCIA, the Vice City airport. Early guides report the method is to steal a docked passenger jet and fly about 1 km away from the airport. Go in on foot or in a fast vehicle, get to a docked jet without drawing too much heat, take off, and keep flying until the trophy pops — roughly a kilometre out, by the guides' account. Unverified in-game, so treat the distance as a guide, not a guarantee.

Early guides report the method is to steal a tank from Mile Zero Air Station and take out enemies while inside it. Expect heavy resistance at a military site, so go in with a plan for the approach and the escape, and use the tank's own firepower once you are in the driver's seat.

Go quietly — no alarms, no witnesses, no wanted level during the job. If you are seen, leave and try again rather than fighting through it, since detection is what the trophy forbids.

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape each time — PSN tracks the count as 0/5, and the 100% checklist reportedly asks for 8, so five is not the end of vaults. Early guides report the chain starts with the optional Chapter 4 mission 'That's Where The Money Is…', after which you follow a security van into a bank while its vault is open. Expect 4 stars on the escape and have a fast bike ready. Do the Chapter 4 mission when it appears, then work through the remaining vaults one by one.

trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks travel the roads of Leonida in free roam — watch for one, stop it, crack it open and grab the cash, then lose whatever wanted level follows. The 'classic blitz' name nods to the series' old heist style, so a fast getaway vehicle parked nearby is the whole trick: hit the truck, take the money, and be gone before the response arrives.

Take a plane or helicopter on a sweep of the state, watch the map fill in, and then mop up any grey patches on foot or by car. It pairs naturally with the travel you do for every other trophy.
